candidates.name: Restart Manager Functions
verified_facts: Restart Manager exposes session, resource registration, affected-process query, and session cleanup functions
Shutdown and restart functions are separate from read-only inventory functions
semantic_limits: API availability does not prove an F-host session was run or that any receipt is valid

candidates.name: RmStartSession
verified_facts: RmStartSession creates a Restart Manager session and returns a handle and session key
A session must be ended with RmEndSession
semantic_limits: Starting a diagnostic session changes local Restart Manager state and must be bounded and cleaned up

candidates.name: RmRegisterResources
verified_facts: Resources can be registered by full file name, service short name, or RM_UNIQUE_PROCESS
Related resources should be grouped rather than registered one call per file
semantic_limits: Registration identifies resources for analysis but does not prove which process currently owns them

candidates.name: RmGetList
verified_facts: RmGetList returns applications and services using registered resources
ERROR_MORE_DATA requires resizing the RM_PROCESS_INFO buffer and retrying
semantic_limits: Returned processes require PID plus start-time correlation before owner conclusions

candidates.name: RmEndSession
verified_facts: RmEndSession closes a Restart Manager session
The session handle becomes invalid after cleanup
semantic_limits: Session cleanup does not prove the earlier inventory was complete or fresh

candidates.name: RM_PROCESS_INFO
verified_facts: RM_PROCESS_INFO describes an affected application or service and includes process identity and status
Application type and restartability are separate fields
semantic_limits: A descriptive record does not prove current liveness after the query completes

candidates.name: RM_UNIQUE_PROCESS
verified_facts: RM_UNIQUE_PROCESS combines a process identifier with process start time
The pair reduces ambiguity caused by PID reuse
semantic_limits: PID and start time still require command-line, image-path, and task-owner correlation

candidates.name: RM_REBOOT_REASON
verified_facts: RM_REBOOT_REASON identifies reasons Restart Manager reports a restart as necessary
The value is a bitmask and multiple reasons can be present
semantic_limits: A reboot reason is diagnostic and must not trigger an automatic reboot in this workflow

candidates.name: Wait Chain Traversal
verified_facts: Wait Chain Traversal retrieves resource-dependency chains for threads
Synchronous sessions can block the caller while asynchronous sessions use a callback
semantic_limits: A wait chain is a point-in-time diagnostic and does not by itself prove a deadlock

candidates.name: OpenThreadWaitChainSession
verified_facts: OpenThreadWaitChainSession creates synchronous or asynchronous WCT sessions
Failure returns a null handle and extended error is available through GetLastError
semantic_limits: A session must be closed and bounded to avoid adding another unbounded wait

candidates.name: GetThreadWaitChain
verified_facts: GetThreadWaitChain returns wait nodes and an IsCycle result for a thread
NodeCount is an in-out buffer count and flags control COM/thread behavior
semantic_limits: A reported cycle requires process/thread identity and repeated-sample confirmation

candidates.name: CloseThreadWaitChainSession
verified_facts: CloseThreadWaitChainSession closes the WCT session
Closing an asynchronous session cancels outstanding operations
semantic_limits: Cleanup success does not establish that all callbacks or diagnostics were consumed

candidates.name: WAITCHAIN_NODE_INFO
verified_facts: WAITCHAIN_NODE_INFO describes either a thread node or synchronization-object node
Object status and type must be interpreted with the node union
semantic_limits: Node names can be absent and must not be treated as proof of no wait object

candidates.name: WCT_OBJECT_TYPE
verified_facts: WCT_OBJECT_TYPE classifies thread, mutex, critical-section, COM, process-wait, and other nodes
Different object types require different owner-correlation logic
semantic_limits: Classification does not establish that the object belongs to the canonical runner
